title: Castro's Ring Test: Two New Skills, and the Gymnasts Built for Them
dek: Rings take center stage midday Sunday with two skills the Games have never tested. The whole field owns the base and has two weeks to drill them, so this is not a wildcard: it rewards the real gymnasts. We checked every athlete's background.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Dave Castro revealed two never-before-tested ring gymnastics skills for a midday Sunday event: a ring muscle-up into a forward roll to support, and a backward roll to support. The whole field already owns the base movements and has two weeks to drill the new ones, so it is not a wildcard. We researched every athlete's real gymnastics background to see who is positioned.

blocks.text: Dave Castro just handed the 2026 Games a curveball. On the **Girls Unfiltered** podcast and in a social post demoed by Trista Smith and Jacob Marlow, he unveiled **two ring gymnastics skills the Games have never tested**: a **ring muscle-up straight into a forward roll**, finishing locked out in a support at the top, and a **backward roll to support** with the arms locked out on the rings. Both land **midday Sunday**, the final day, when athletes are deepest into fatigue. His message was blunt: control and strength on the rings will help decide the Fittest on Earth.
What the Two Skills Actually Are

The first chains a **ring muscle-up**, already a Games staple, directly into a **forward roll** on the rings, ending locked out in support at the top: one continuous, high-control sequence rather than a stop-and-reset. The second, the **backward roll to support**, is a still-rings skill where the athlete rolls backward through the rings to finish in a straight-arm support. It is rare in CrossFit but a **staple of the United Grid League**, where teams drill it. CrossFit's own coaching notes list real prerequisites for it: confident ring dips, a strict muscle-up, and genuine body control. These are not volume movements. They are precision under fatigue.
Why This Rewards the Gymnasts, Not a Wildcard

Here is the part that got called a wildcard, and why that misses. **Every athlete in this field already owns the base these skills are built on**: strict ring muscle-ups, skin-the-cats, and strict ring handstand push-ups. The two new pieces are **additions on top of that base, not a foreign language**. And nobody walks in cold: the field has roughly **two weeks to drill them**. So this is not a skill nobody can do. It is a skill everyone can build, which turns it into a test of **who builds it fastest and cleanest**, and that rewards a real gymnastics background and the sharpest ring control. Two weeks is enough time to make it a show, not a wipeout.
We Checked the Backgrounds

Our model scores gymnastics off this season's results, and a season score can miss a real gymnast having an off year. So we went past the model and **researched every athlete's actual background**: who was a competitive artistic gymnast, a tumbler or trampolinist, a diver, a parkour athlete, or a known rings specialist. The list reshuffled. On the men's side the top of the read is **three genuine former gymnasts**. **Patrick Vellner** competed on apparatus into 2010 and is the field's cleanest technician. **Victor Hoffer** trained federation-level artistic gymnastics in France from age 3, roughly 20 hours a week; his 44 gymnastics score this season badly undersells him and this event is built for him. **Roman Khrennikov** came through a Russian Olympic-reserve gymnastics program plus break-dancing floorwork. Behind them sit the sharpest technicians: **Justin Medeiros**, whose wrestling gives a direct rolling instinct, and **Colten Mertens**, who plays in the United Grid League where the backward roll to support is a standard skill, so one of the two new movements may not be new to him at all.

The women's read moved even more. The model's proxy favored big bodyweight-strength numbers, but **strength is not the same as rotation**. The athletes built for this are the real gymnasts and ring specialists: **Madeline Sturt**, Australia's premier rings athlete, whose 47 gymnastics score completely hides her ring control; **Abigail Domit**, a USAG Level 9 artistic gymnast; **Ella Wilkinson**, who tumbled and trampolined for Team GB to age 15; **Danielle Brandon**, a childhood gymnast and state diver; and **Haley Adams** and **Alexis Raptis**, both former competitive artistic gymnasts. A powerful athlete without that background can still grind these out, but the rolls look sharpest on the athletes who have been rolling and inverting since childhood.

blocks.text: A season gym score misses a real gymnast having a quiet year. Five the number underrates: **Victor Hoffer** (44) trained artistic gymnastics from age 3; **Colten Mertens** (56) drills the backward roll to support in the Grid league; **Madeline Sturt** (47) and **Matilde Garnes** (47) are ring specialists; **Ella Wilkinson** (57) competed in tumbling for Team GB. blocks.title: Methodology
blocks.text: This read is built from researched gymnastics backgrounds, not a single model number. For every athlete we checked bios, interviews and federation records for a real gymnastics, tumbling, diving, or rings-specialist history, and weighted that over the season gymnastics score, because a former gymnast predicts fast, clean acquisition of a novel ring skill better than one season's percentile does. Where we could not confirm a background, we did not guess. These two movements have never been tested at the Games, so this ranks who is positioned to learn them fastest and cleanest, not a predicted result. Reveal via the Girls Unfiltered podcast and Castro's social post.

title: Day 1 of the 2026 Games Is Five Events. Who Survives Them All?
dek: The Games open at the Ranch with a metcon, a 7.2km run and three max lifts, all in one day. We modeled who has the breadth to survive it, and who gets exposed.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The 2026 CrossFit Games open with five scored events on Day 1 (Wednesday July 22): The 2007 Hopper, Ranch 7200 and The CrossFit Total. We built a Day-1 breadth score from the model to find who covers a metcon, a 7.2km run and three max lifts best, and who gets exposed by the day's contradictions.

blocks.text: The 2026 Games do not ease anyone in. On **Day 1, Wednesday July 22**, at the off-site venues around the Ranch in Aromas, the individual field faces **five scored events**: **The 2007 Hopper** (Event 1, a row-and-rig metcon), **Ranch 7200** (Event 2, a 7,200-meter trail run), and **The CrossFit Total** (Events 3-5, max back squat, shoulder press and deadlift). A metcon, an endurance run, and a strength triple, all before anyone touches the SAP Center floor. It is the broadest opening day the Games have programmed, and the demands actively fight each other.
The Contradiction Built Into Day 1

Look at what these five events ask for. The Hopper wants a gymnastics engine and grip. Ranch 7200 wants a deep aerobic motor and a **light frame** to carry over 4.5 miles. The Total wants the opposite: raw, **absolute strength**, where more body mass is an asset. A 65 kg runner and a 100 kg squatter are almost different species, and Day 1 asks every athlete to be both. Nobody wins all five. The athlete who wins the day is the one with no hole for it to find, so we scored the field on breadth: how well each covers all six domains these events tax, weighted 70 percent on the average and 30 percent on their single weakest domain, because one crack is fatal when the day tests everything.
The Men: Medeiros Is Built for This

Run the five events through the model and one name sits on top: **Justin Medeiros**. The two-time champion reads top-three in the metcon, the run, and the strength triple, and he has **no soft domain, nothing below the 77th percentile** across gymnastics, engine, monostructural, aerobic, heavy strength and Olympic lifting. That is the definition of a Day-1 athlete. **Roman Khrennikov** is right behind on a monster engine and elite lifting; his only relative give is the long run, the one event where his size is a tax. **Ricky Garard** has no weak domain either, while **Patrick Vellner** pairs huge gymnastics and strength with the one crack the run can widen, his engine.

blocks.text: The Women: Lawson's Balance, Adams's Gamble

The women's read splits into engines and all-arounders. **Emma Lawson** tops the breadth score because she has no weakness, nothing under the 67th percentile across all five events. **Haley Adams** and **Lucy Campbell** own the two biggest engines in the field and should lead the Hopper and the run, but they share the same hole: the back squat and deadlift. The Total is where the strength day claws back what they bank early. **Mirjam von Rohr** is the interesting one, pairing the field's best raw engine with a record-setting back squat, the rare woman who can score on the run AND the strength, which is why the model likes her Day-1 shape.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Back at the Ranch

The venue is the story too. Day 1 runs at the Aromas ranch, the birthplace of the Games from 2007 to 2009, and the programming leans all the way into it: the 2007 Hopper revives the very first Games event, and the original hopper apparatus is back. Opening the sport's 20th-anniversary Games where it started, with a run on the same dirt, is a deliberate homecoming before the lights of San Jose take over July 24-26.

blocks.title: Methodology
blocks.text: The Day-1 breadth score blends each athlete's model percentile across the six domains these five events tax (gymnastics, long engine, monostructural, aerobic, heavy strength and Olympic lifting), weighted 70 percent on the average and 30 percent on the weakest of those domains, since a single hole is costly when the day tests everything. Percentiles come from official 2026 Open and Quarterfinals results plus all prior Games; the strength reads fold in real competition maxes. This ranks Day-1 breadth, not a predicted finish.

title: The CrossFit Total: Who Tops Each Lift, and the Whole Thing
dek: Events 3, 4 and 5 are three 50-point lifts. We pulled the athletes real competition maxes and built a leaderboard for each, plus the overall Total.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Events 3-5 of the 2026 CrossFit Games are The CrossFit Total: 1RM back squat, shoulder press and deadlift, each a 50-point event. We built a leaderboard for every lift from real competition maxes (the 2025 Games back squat, the 2023 Rogue deadlift, the 2020 Games press) plus reported PRs and labeled estimates, then summed them for the overall Total.

blocks.text: Events 3, 4 and 5 are **The CrossFit Total**, three separate 50-point events: a 1-rep-max back squat, strict shoulder press and deadlift. So instead of guessing, we went to the tape. We pulled these athletes actual competition maxes, the **2025 CrossFit Games 1-rep-max back squat**, the **2023 Rogue Invitational** and **2026 World Fitness Project** max deadlifts, and the strict presses from the **2020 Games Total**, then filled the gaps with official reported PRs and clearly labeled self-reported stats. Here is a leaderboard for every lift, and for the whole Total. Absolute load wins; bodyweight does not factor into the score.
Event 3, the Back Squat

**Colten Mertens** owns this one on real evidence: he **won the 2025 Games 1-rep-max back squat at 570 lb**, breaking an 18-year Games record. **Nick Mathew** (555) and **Justin Medeiros** (512) also squatted big in that same 2025 test; **Austin Hatfield** (535) and **Guilherme Malheiros** (511) sit on reported PRs. The women are led by another 2025 Games result: **Mirjam von Rohr won that event at 360 lb**, with **Anikha Greer** tied second at 355, then **Elisa Fuliano** (353) and **Kyra Milligan** (340) on profile numbers.

blocks.text: Event 4, the Shoulder Press (the honest board)

Here is the one to read with a raised eyebrow. Almost nobody has a real strict-press number, because CrossFit rarely tests it. Only a handful exist: **Jeffrey Adler pressed 207 lb at the 2020 Games**, **Justin Medeiros 175** and **Patrick Vellner ~200** in a Total, **Haley Adams 127** at the 2020 Games, and **Alex Gazan** owns a 167 lb training PR. Everyone else is an estimate off their overhead strength, so we tag those. On that basis **Roman Khrennikov** projects the biggest press in the field (an estimated 240), with **Dallin Pepper** next; among the women **Hannah Black** and **Gazan** lead. Treat this board as informed projection, not fact.

blocks.text: Event 5, the Deadlift

The deadlift has the best competition record of the three, thanks to the 2023 Rogue Invitational and, new this year, the 2026 World Fitness Project max-deadlift events. **Patrick Vellner (595) and Tudor Magda (595)** went head to head at Rogue; **Nick Mathew** matches 605 on his profile and **Justin Medeiros** pulled **600** in competition. On the women's side the board just moved. **Aimee Cringle** pulled a competition-verified **197 kg (435 lb)** at World Fitness Project Tour Stop 1 in May 2026, tied second in that field and well above the 408 she self-reports; **Matilde Garnes** hit **193 kg (425)** at the same event (single-source, provisional). They edge **Alex Gazan**, whose **425 lb won the 2023 Rogue max deadlift** and is still the most bulletproof number here. **Madeline Sturt** (408) and **Hannah Black** (400) hold on self-reported PRs. One correction worth flagging: our earlier 405 for **Mirjam von Rohr** was an estimate. Her only meet-verified pull is 380 lb and she did not contest the WFP deadlift, so she drops out of the top five.

Sum the three lifts and the men's Total is led by **Nick Mathew** at roughly **1,355 lb** (555 squat, a big deadlift at 605, and an estimated press), with **Colten Mertens** (record squat), **Justin Medeiros**, **Roman Khrennikov** and **Jayson Hopper** bunched around 1,285-1,290. title: Event 1 Is the 2007 Hopper. Whose Profile Fits It?
dek: The opener revives the 2007 opener. We modeled whose profile the row, pull-ups and push jerks reward.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Event 1 of the 2026 CrossFit Games is The 2007 Hopper: a 1,000m row then 5 rounds of 25 pull-ups and 7 push jerks. We modeled whose profile the workout rewards, with a data-grounded top 5 for men and women.

blocks.text: Event 1 pulls a fossil out of the vault. It is **The 2007 Hopper**, the workout that opened the very first CrossFit Games: a 1,000-meter row, then 5 rounds of 25 pull-ups and 7 push jerks, for time. The barbell sits at 135 lb for the men and 85 lb for the women. Everything else is you against gravity. The row and the pull-ups carry no load at all. Individuals kick it off Wednesday, July 22, 2026. Read the pieces and the shape is clear: this is a medium-length grind, not a sprint and not a marathon. The 2007 winner needed about 13 minutes; when the field ran it back in 2013 the top time dropped to 8:33. The engine gets lit early on the rower, then the day becomes a math problem, 125 total pull-ups against 35 light push jerks. The barbell is almost a formality. Whoever can cycle pull-ups in big unbroken chunks while breathing hard controls this.
The Men: Two Co-Favorites, One Light Barbell

The model likes **Roman Khrennikov** and **Justin Medeiros** at the top, and they sit within about two points of each other. Treat them as co-favorites, because the order hinges on how much you weight that light barbell. Khrennikov leads on the strength of a **90 Bodyweight** score paired with an **81 Metabolic** and a **79 Long Engine**, the exact three things this workout hammers. Medeiros trails by a hair with the more even card: **80 Weightlifting**, **77 Gymnastics**, **78 Metabolic**. If the 135 lb push jerk matters more than the fatigue math suggests, Medeiros closes the gap and passes him. Behind the two, Ricky Garard, Patrick Vellner, and James Sprague are bunched. Garard's profile is balanced with no soft spot on the bodyweight side (77). Vellner owns the best gymnastics number in this group at 78 but the lowest long engine at 66, so a longer grind works against him. Sprague, the youngest read here, is carried by a 79 Bodyweight and steady metabolic work.

blocks.text: The Women: Engine and Grip Up Top

On the women's side **Haley Adams** heads the read, and it is not close on the domains that count. Her **85 Bodyweight** and **82 Long Engine** are built for 125 pull-ups inside a medium time cap, and a 79 Metabolic keeps her moving between sets. Lucy Campbell is right behind with the best pure gymnastics score in the group at **83**, plus an 80 Long Engine, so the pull-ups should come fast and stay smooth. Emma Lawson is the steady one, nothing below 75 across the taxed domains, which is why she lands third. Mirjam von Rohr is the interesting name: she matches Adams' **82 Long Engine** and posts a 79 Bodyweight, but her 69 Metabolic and 70 Gymnastics keep her fourth on this specific workout. Danielle Brandon rounds out the five with solid all-around marks dragged down by a 67 Long Engine, the one number that a medium grind will find.

blocks.title: How to Read This
blocks.text: These are not predictions of the result. Each ranking is an athlete's mean measured placement percentile, the percent of the 60-athlete field they beat, on exactly the domains this event taxes: Metabolic, Gymnastics, Bodyweight, and Long Engine, with weightlifting kept light. The scores come from the official 2026 Open, Quarterfinals, and all prior Games. The event line tells you what the workout is; the top-five tells you whose profile fits it. On the men's side Khrennikov (79.8) and Medeiros (77.8) sit within about two points, so treat them as co-favorites and let the light barbell decide the order. A great fit still has to be executed on the floor Wednesday.

title: Event 2 Is a 7,200m Ranch Run. Whose Engine Fits It?
dek: The second event sends the field off-road for a 7.2km trail run. We modeled whose aerobic engine, and whose body mass, the Ranch rewards.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Event 2 of the 2026 CrossFit Games is Ranch 7200: a 7,200-meter trail run at the Aromas ranch where the Games were born. We modeled whose profile a long run rewards, scaling the aerobic read by power-to-weight, with a data-grounded top 5 for men and women.

blocks.text: Event 2 takes the 2026 CrossFit Games off-road. On the opening day at the Aromas ranch, the patch of California where the Games were born in 2007, the field faces **Ranch 7200**: a 7,200-meter trail run, for time. That is about 4.5 miles of dirt and hills. It is the purest endurance test the Games have run in years, and it rewards two things a barbell never asks for: a deep aerobic engine and a light frame to carry it. Individuals run it Wednesday, July 22, right after the opener.
A Run Rewrites the Board

Here is the honest problem with modeling a run: nothing in the 2026 season was a run. The Open and Quarterfinals were indoor, machine-and-barbell affairs, so we do not have a measured 7km time for anyone. What we do have is each athlete's long engine (sustained output), their monostructural machine output, and their oxidative-system score, all computed from real results. That is the right starting point. Then we adjust for the one thing a trail run punishes that a rower does not: body mass. Over 7.2km, every extra kilogram is a kilogram carried the whole way. So the read below is an aerobic-engine ranking scaled by power-to-weight, not a stopwatch.
The Men: Adler's Frame Beats Khrennikov's Engine

The biggest engine in the men's field belongs to **Roman Khrennikov**, an 81 monostructural with elite sustained output. On a rower or a bike, he wins this. But at a corrected **103 kilograms**, a 7.2km run is where his size is a bill that comes due, and the mass-adjusted read drops him to the back of the top five. The pick at the top is **Justin Medeiros**: a 79 oxidative engine on an **88-kilogram** frame, the best blend of motor and manageable mass in the field. **Ricky Garard** (corrected 93 kg) and **James Sprague** (95 kg) follow on strong engines. **Jeffrey Adler** slots **fourth, not first**: his weight was mis-listed at 72 kg but the official record is **197 lb (89 kg)**, essentially Medeiros's mass without the same aerobic ceiling, so the run is a hold-serve event for him rather than the runaway an earlier read implied.

blocks.text: The Women: Adams Runs Away From the Field

On the women's side it is not close. **Haley Adams** owns the single biggest engine in either division, an 82 long engine, and carries it at 64 kilograms. Best motor, lightest relevant frame: on a run, that is the dream combination, and she is the clear model pick. **Emma Lawson**, also 64 kilograms with a balanced aerobic card, is second. **Mirjam von Rohr** posts the field's highest raw engine score at 83 and lands third; a long run is the kind of event where her sustained output can shine even against lighter athletes. **Lucy Campbell** (81 engine) and **Danielle Brandon** (75 monostructural, and a better runner than her reputation) complete the five.

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Back at the Ranch

Opening here is not a gimmick, it is a homecoming. The Ranch in Aromas hosted the first three CrossFit Games from 2007 to 2009, on Dave Castro's family property, until the sport outgrew the field. Trail running is woven through Games history too: a roughly seven-kilometer trail run opened Games competition in 2016. Ranch 7200 stitches both threads together, the birthplace and the run, onto the opening day of the sport's 20th-anniversary Games, right alongside the revived 2007 Hopper that runs as Event 1.

blocks.title: Methodology
blocks.text: There was no run in the 2026 season, so no athlete has a measured 7km time. This read starts from competition-derived performance profiles, long engine (sustained output), monostructural (machine and cardio), and oxidative (aerobic system), each a placement percentile from official 2026 Open and Quarterfinals results plus all prior Games. Because a 7.2km run also rewards a light frame, we scale that aerobic score by power-to-weight using each athlete's body mass. It is a fit read for a run, not a predicted finish. A great profile still has to be run on the dirt Wednesday.

title: What Dave Castro Has Already Told Us About the 2026 Games
dek: The hopper is back for a live Friday-night draw, swimming moves to a pool, and the Ranch is lurking. A sourced rundown of every reveal and tease.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: A sourced rundown of what Dave Castro has revealed and teased about the 2026 CrossFit Games programming: the returning hopper, a pool swim, cycling, the Rogue Pig and Snail, and the Ranch.

blocks.text: Dave Castro tells you about the Games for months before they start, in teasers, ranch videos and offhand comments. The trick is separating what is **confirmed** from what is a hint, because he plants misdirection on purpose. Here is what we actually know about the 2026 programming, with the source on every line.
The headline: the original hopper returns

Castro announced that the original Games hopper, the old peanut roaster used to pick the very first workout at the Ranch in 2007, is back. A workout gets **drawn live from it on the morning of Friday, July 24** and tested on the individuals under the lights at SAP Center that night. Athletes reacted fast: Taylor Self called it sick, and Jayson Hopper wrote, "let me pull from it, its only right."
Confirmed

items: **Swimming is back, in a pool.** Not open water. Presented by TYR, most likely at the Morgan Hill Outdoor Sport Center, the 2020 Games swim venue.
**Cycling returns** as part of the individual off-site opening, in the Games tradition of a Ride bike test. Distance and bike not yet announced.

**The competition is four days for individuals: Wednesday July 22 through Sunday July 26.** It opens at off-site Bay Area locations on the 22nd, livestreamed but not open to the public, before three arena days at SAP Center.
**The Rogue Pig and Snail return.** The Pig is a heavy rubber-encased block; the Snail is shaped like a hay bale but partly filled with sand that shifts as it rolls.
**20 scored events, the most in Games history**, on the Games 20th anniversary.

blocks.text: Teased (read with caution)

items: **Big Bob, on the street.** Walking SAP Center, Castro floated a team drag race "sprinting Big Bob down Barack Obama" Boulevard, calling it epic. A hint, not a confirmation.
**An outdoor run on closed roads.** He measured a turnaround about 200 yards down Barack Obama Boulevard with a trundle wheel, hinting at a roughly 400-yard looped street course.

**Extra days at the Ranch.** Castro said three SAP Center days does not mean a three-day Games: there "could be additional days that are not available for spectators to watch," read widely as non-spectator competition at the Aromas ranch.
**A possibly-new movement.** Asked if 2026 brings a new movement, he said he does not believe truly new movements exist, but on a previously-unprogrammed one answered "Possibly."
**A programming handoff.** On a CF Network show he said he is considering handing event programming to someone else this year, without naming who.

blocks.text: The throughline is the Ranch. Two Behind the Scenes videos show Castro testing 2026 events with athlete Rafael Sancen at Aromas in the weeks before the Games, so whatever lands in San Jose is being prototyped on the same dirt where the hopper was first drawn in 2007.

title: Who Actually Has the Engine to Win San Jose?
dek: The aerobic engines most likely to hold up across 20 events and 4 days.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: The 2026 CrossFit Games qualifiers with the strongest aerobic engine, ranked by oxidative, monostructural and sustained-output performance percentiles from official competition results.

blocks.text: San Jose is 20 scored events over 4 days, July 24-26. That format does not reward one big lift or one fast sprint. It rewards the athlete whose output holds up on day four the same way it did on day one. So before we argue about who wins, ask a narrower question: who actually has the engine to survive it? The numbers below answer that, using only aerobic-system, monostructural, and sustained-output performance profiles.
The Men: Two Names Tied at the Top

Justin Medeiros and Roman Khrennikov share the highest oxidative score in the men's field at **79.3**. They get there differently. Khrennikov pairs that with the best monostructural mark of any man here at 80.7 and a sustained-output score of 78.5, the engine of a two-time Games runner-up who grinds rather than fades. Medeiros sits a hair behind on the machine work (77.8) but his profile is the most balanced of the group, with capacity at 78.9 and a Games title already on the record.

blocks.text: The interesting case is James Sprague. His oxidative number (71.5) is fifth among these men, but his projected rank of 4 is the best in the group. His engine score of 73.6 actually outruns his overall capacity of 70.2, which tells you the aerobic side is carrying him further than his average event finish suggests. Khrennikov is the inverse: the best engine among the men attached to a projected rank of 15, a reminder that a profile is not a placement. Patrick Vellner is the one to flag with caution. The aerobic read is strong at 74.6, but his sustained-output score sags to 65.5, the lowest of the six, the kind of split that gets found in a 20-event grind.
The Women: The Champion Type Versus the Top Seed

On the women's side the oxidative leader is Haley Adams at **76.0**, and she does not stop there. Her sustained-output score of 81.9 is the highest engine number in either division, paired with a 79.3 on the machines. A four-time Games athlete, she profiles as the kind of competitor a long format favors. What stands out is the gap: Adams projects 13th overall, yet no one in this group has a bigger engine. The format she is walking into is the one that should narrow that gap.

blocks.text: Lucy Campbell carries the highest projected rank in this group at 2, and her engine backs it: 80.4 on sustained output, second only to Adams. The standout split belongs to Mirjam von Rohr. Her oxidative score is the lowest of the five women at 71.3, but her engine reads 81.7, near the top of the field, and she projects first overall. That is a profile built on holding output rather than topping the aerobic ladder. Worth a note on Danielle Brandon: solid machine work at 74.6, but her engine of 67.2 is the lowest among these women, the same fade-risk pattern we flagged on the men's side.
What the Engine Tells You About San Jose

items: The aerobic leaders, Medeiros and Khrennikov for the men, Adams for the women, depend least on a single good day.

Two athletes have engines that outrank their projected finish: Sprague (engine 73.6, proj. rank 4) and von Rohr (engine 81.7, proj. rank 1). In a 20-event format, that sustained output tends to show up late, not early.
The fade risk lives in the engine column, not the oxidative one: Vellner (65.5) and Brandon (67.2) read well aerobically but lowest on sustained output among their peers.

These are competition-derived performance profiles, not lab measurements, and projected ranks are profiles, not predictions.

title: Swimming and Cycling Are Back. Whose Profile Wins?
dek: Two monostructural events return. The model says who that helps.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: Swimming and cycling return to the 2026 CrossFit Games. A profile-fit read of which qualifiers the monostructural and engine demands reward, built from the Persistence Athletics model.

blocks.text: CrossFit confirmed it this offseason: swimming is back at the 2026 Games (reported by The Barbell Spin), and cycling returns too (per CrossFit Games). The format is 20 scored events across four days in San Jose, July 24 to 26. Both tests pull on the same two places: the monostructural domain (cardio and machines) and the engine, sustained output over time. So which profiles get rewarded, and which suddenly have a problem to solve?

One honest caveat first. **There is no swim event in this data**, and nobody here has a measured swim split. What we have are placement percentiles from the 2026 Open, Quarterfinals, and every prior Games. Treat the swim read as a proxy: a strong monostructural and engine score says an athlete moves efficiently and holds output when the clock gets long, which is most of what open-water work demands. The cycling read is firmer, because that is squarely machine and engine territory the data covers.
Men: whose profile fits

At the top of the men's board, Roman Khrennikov pairs an 80.7 monostructural percentile with a 78.5 engine for a 79.6 fit, a heavy-engine build that does not flinch at long cardio. But keep fit and overall projection separate: Khrennikov fits best while projecting 15th, while Jeffrey Adler sits fifth here yet carries the strongest projected finish at second.

blocks.text: Who feels the pressure

The flip side is a matter of principle, not a name to mock. Added long cardio hits the load, strength, and skill-leaning profiles hardest, whose edge lives in a heavy barbell or a high-skill gymnastics piece rather than sustained output. That is a specialization, not a flaw. But a swim-bike menu narrows the room a specialist has to bank points, so the cardio days are where offseason work goes.

items: Reward: balanced builds high in mono and engine, like Khrennikov (79.6) and Adams (80.6).
Engine-first works too: von Rohr and Campbell clear 80 on engine despite lower mono.
Pressure: load, strength, and skill profiles have less room to bank points on cardio days.
Reminder: fit ranks the swim-bike days, not the whole event; Adler and von Rohr project best overall.

title: Prep Watch: 10 Days Out, What the Whole Field Is Drilling
dek: The 2026 field is deep in final prep and posting it. Here is what every revealed test demands, the ring skills everyone is grinding, and who our model reads as built for the hottest movement of the weekend.
author: Ravikant Dewangan
summary: With the 2026 CrossFit Games about 10 days out (competition July 22-26, San Jose), athletes are deep in final prep and the training content is everywhere. Dave Castro has revealed enough - the CrossFit Total, a 7.2km Ranch trail run, a returning pool, and two never-tested ring skills - that the field's focus is clear. We break down what is hot, what each test demands, and who our model reads as built for it.

blocks.text: Ten days out from San Jose and the 2026 field is in the loud part of prep, all over your feed. The reason it is easy to read what they are drilling: **Dave Castro has already tipped most of the weekend.** We know Events 3, 4 and 5 are the CrossFit Total, Event 2 is a 7.2km Ranch trail run, a pool is back in play, and Sunday hides two ring skills the Games have never tested. Here is what is hot, what each test actually asks for, and who our model reads as built for it.
What's Hot: The Ring Skills

The single biggest talking point of the buildup is the pair of still-rings skills Castro unveiled on July 10: a **ring muscle-up straight into a forward roll to support**, and a **backward roll to support**. Here is the tell on how much the field cares: the reveal actually landed *after* athletes had already been spotted testing the movements on Instagram, and CrossFit followed with an official movement feature. Nobody is walking in cold. The whole field already owns the base - strict ring muscle-ups, skin-the-cats, strict ring handstand push-ups - and has had two weeks to drill the two additions, so this is not a wildcard nobody can do. It rewards the sharpest gymnasts and the cleanest technicians.
The Run Nobody Got to Train Indoors

Event 2, **Ranch 7200**, is a 7,200-meter trail run for time on the Aromas hills, about 4.5 miles of dirt and climbing. The catch that explains all the trail-miles content right now: the entire 2026 season was indoor, machine-and-barbell racing, so nobody has a measured trail time. On corrected competition vitals our model reads **Justin Medeiros** at the top on the best engine-to-mass blend, ahead of Ricky Garard and James Sprague. The biggest engine in the field, Roman Khrennikov, pays a real mass tax over 4.5 miles of climbing.
The Total: It's Max-Out Season

Events 3 to 5 are **The CrossFit Total**: a 1-rep-max back squat, strict shoulder press and deadlift, each scored as its own 50-point event. That is why the prep footage is full of heavy singles. The women's deadlift board just got a real-competition refresh - **Aimee Cringle** pulled 197 kg (435 lb) at the World Fitness Project - while the men's Total leans on **Nick Mathew**'s size. The strict press is the wild card: almost nobody in the field has real strict-press data, so it is the single lift most likely to scramble the order.
And a Pool Is Back

CrossFit confirmed swimming returns in a controlled pool for 2026, which pulls the proven water athletes back into the conversation after years of the swim being an open-water lottery. In a pool, technique and turns reward the handful of genuine swimmers in the field rather than the biggest engine.
Who to Watch on the Hot Skill

items: **Patrick Vellner and Victor Hoffer (men)** - the field's two former competitive artistic gymnasts. The new rolls are the closest thing to home court for anyone here; Hoffer trained federation-level gymnastics from age 3.
**Madeline Sturt and Abigail Domit (women)** - a rings specialist with teaching-level control and a USAG Level 9 artistic gymnast. Rotation and support are second nature.
**Colten Mertens** - plays in the United Grid League, where the backward roll to support is a standard skill. One of the two "new" movements may not be new to him at all.
**Roman Khrennikov** - an Olympic-reserve gymnastics base makes the rings a strength; his one tax this weekend is the run, not the rolls.

blocks.text: Every read here is our model plus Castro's verified reveals, not a result prediction. The ring-skill watch list weights researched gymnastics backgrounds over a single season score, since a real gymnast picks up a novel ring skill faster than a percentile predicts. Full breakdowns for each event are in The Breakdown.
